subject: Spring Creek Meeting
comment: Spring Creek Neighborhood Meeting October 3, 2020 Zoom Format The meeting began at 9am conducted by Mary Millar Spring Creek Chair and facilitated by Karen Tapahe Provo City Neighborhood Coordinator. Approximately 15 attended. Item 1 George Bills of Gardner and Associates requests the rezoning of approximately 8.5 acres from Heavy Commercial (CM), Residential Agricultural (RA), One-Family Residential (R1.6 and R1.10), and Agricultural (A1.5) to the Medium Density Residential (MDR) zone, as well as concept plan approval, to facilitate the construction of 204 dwelling units (30 townhomes, 30 studio apartments, 64 2- bedroom apartments, and 80 1-bedroom apartments), located at approximately 1724 S State Street. Developer Don Mullen presented his plat plans and elevations for the above proposed housing project Concerns discussed included: Is the drainage including the catch basin in the north west corner sufficient for the development.? Mr Mullen stated that the drainage plan had been approved by the city engineering department What are the new traffic considerations given the twice daily traffic influx at the adjacent school? It is recommended that the exiting traffic use 1640 South to access State Street. The developer will be required to improve the south side of 1640 South along their property. A new traffic study has been conducted and indicated everything was good to go. The number of living units is stated as 204 Mr Mullen stated that parking for the development has been approved as sufficient. The developer will provide signs indicating the school property is not to be used for parking at any time. A representative for the school stated that there are mandates for the number of parking spaces the school is required to have and currently they are short. Mr Mullen stated that the current property owner has a parking easement on some area of his property but it is unclear where that is. The final use of the project as apartments or condominiums has not been definitively decided, --likely will be after final plat approval. 1 Item 2 Jodi Hoffman requests a zone change from A1.5 (agricultural) to SC2 (community shopping center) zone, located at 1724 S State Street in the Spring Creek Neighborhood to allow the charter school to be used as a preschool and for recreational use. The property currently houses Treeside Charter School within two buildings. The owner and developer of the property is seeking a rezone to facilitate the continued use of the property should the charter school cease its lease of the two buildings. The property owner foresees an easy use transition for the property if, at a minimum, preschool and recreational uses are permitted in the zone. Applicant states that the larger building would most effectively be used as an indoor athletic club, with perhaps supporting and related wellness uses, and the smaller school building would most effectively be used as a preschool, uses included in the SC2 zone. This is located at 1724 S State. A representative for Jodi Hoffman presented the request for the above rezone and stated that it is not related to Item 1 for housing development. There are now two buildings used for Treeside Charter School. The land owners are postering for the time when the school no longer occupies the buildings and commercial use can be facilitated by the new zone. Possibilities are a preschool in the north building and a commercial gym in the south building. Concerns discussed included: The traffic patterns will not change with this rezone procedure. The owner feels like the school may be leaving in the near future but stated that the land owner’s relation to Treeside’s position as a lessee is a private matter The city master plan indicates this area is expected to be mixed use in the future. The land owner signed a 25 year lease with Treeside November 2016 and the construction was completed as a school installation. It was at that time zoned under the most restricted permitted use of the land and now it is requested that it be open for any commercial use. Erin Preston, Attorney for Treeside Charter, presented the schools position: She stated that the owner signed with another party for use of the gym near the same time Treeside signed. This resulted in Treeside receiving a citation from the office of education. Treeside changed the locks on the gym area and Provo City later evicted those tenants for zone violations. The effect of this zone change would now allow third parties to occupy the building. The owner has been restrained form further leasing pending current litigation in state court. Treeside stated that there were misrepresentations made in their rezone application which included that the school is leaving. She stated that the school is fully staffed and intends to remain, Treeside’s court filings state that the school will continue to occupy both buildings while school is in session and asks that this matter be deferred until the court case is settled. The applicant representative responded to the above that they are willing to enter into a development agreement with the city for school and athletic use only. She stated that the owner and the school have a pending settlement agreement and that they are not paying their financial obligations. She stated that the school will not be staying for the duration of their lease. 2 Attorney Preston stated that there are two different attorneys representing the owner and that the owner’s representative today may not be aware of other litigation or misrepresentations. Attorney Preston stated that there is no settlement agreement and that their non payment is inaccurate. This would open the door to anything despite the owner’s stated intentions and would create a tool for the owner to use against the school. Bill Farley who is an adjacent land owner stated that in 40 years of dealing with the owner/applicant he has had considerable issues and said, the zoning for the land the school should not change. A Mrs Townsend (did not catch her first name)reports to be an employee of the school stated that the applicants presentation consisted of many half truths and did not represent the employee’s experiences with the school. She stated that the school never agreed to leave and in the future it cannot be operated safely with other building occupants. She stated that the school uses the gym and that random strangers have been found wandering through both buildings. She alluded to the taxpayers ultimately having paid for the building and that there are still leftover problems from previous tenants and the building itself. Karen Tapahee encouraged all to go to the opentownhall.com web site and to review the above three items and that comments can be left there. Item 3 Ryan Livingston is proposing a zone change from the One-Family Residential (R1.10) zone to the Low Density Residential (LDR) zone in order to accommodate single-family and twin homes for a property in the Spring Creek Neighborhood. This is located at approximately 1107 E 1320 South. Brandon Larsen, city planner, from the city introduced that the developer requests a zone change to allow for single family and twin homes on a property adjacent to his current development. The applicant was not in attendance. There were no significant comments on this item, however, residents of Spring Creek Neighborhood have long requested (at several neighborhood meetings over the past five years) some single family homes be built. 3

subject: LaFontaine Property
comment: Planning Commission: I’m writing in regards to the LaFontain development that is coming before you on October 28th. This proposal is for several town homes located in a single family home neighborhood. Our neighborhood has fought for many years to preserve our neighborhood from multi unit dwellings. Our neighborhood consists of many upper end homes and quiet streets. This type of development is not in line with the single family homes that exist here. Neighbors are not in favor it this development. I appreciate the LaFontaine’s as current neighbors, but I do not approve of this development in the neighborhood. This is a small plot of land in the neighborhood. There are too many units for this small area. It would be best if they just wanted to subdivide into 4 lots for 4 single family homes. Access to it is on a “right in, right out” access. I have personally witnessed many cars drying to cross over several lines of traffic on university avenue to come into the “right in” exit using a left turn. This area is zoned Single Family, and we want it to remain Single Family. There is already a beautiful home on this property that they would tear down to put of multiple units. A development like this would adversely affect our property values. Several new homes have just been built across the street from this proposed development and they will be directly affected by this development. They are not in favor of it. It will increase traffic to a quiet neighborhood. The renderings of all the “green space” on their drawings is false and misleading. This is a very small space. This neighborhood is not zoned for multi home developments and we do not want the zoning changed. We want to preserve our neighborhood and keep it to single family homes only. Please put my vote in as “Opposed”. Thank you, Susan Sewell
